_readme: SHARED CURATED ENRICHMENT — hand-written detail layered onto existing spots,
keyed by spot id (the `id` field in data/regions/<region>.json).
WHY: some cards are thin because the open data behind them is thin, and no
dataset will ever fix it. Personal notes (1.12.0) solve that for ONE device;
this file is the version that SHIPS to everyone.
LICENSING — the rule that makes this safe:
WRITE YOUR OWN WORDS. Do NOT paste text from a city, district, park or
business website: that prose is copyrighted even when the facts in it are
not. Facts are free (who runs it, when it opens, that there is a bedrock
mortar site) — sentences are not. Federal sources (RIDB, NRHP, GNIS, USGS,
NOAA) are public domain and their text may be carried, but those already
come in through their own adapters. NEVER copy from social platforms.
`link` should point at the official page so a reader can go read the
original for themselves.
FIELDS (all optional): notes, link, link_label, best_light, best_season,
access_difficulty, subject_type. They only FILL GAPS — anything the
ingested data already provides is left alone, so a future ingest that
improves upstream never gets clobbered by a stale hand-written line.
Entries live under `spots`. Keep this file small and high-quality; it is for
places worth the effort, not for bulk.

fairchild-park-indian-grinding-rocks@9qc.notes: Bedrock mortars ground into the granite outcrop by the Nisenan, who lived along these creek drainages long before the Gold Rush. The holes are easy to walk past — look down at the flat rock rather than out at the trees. Low, raking side-light picks the depressions out; flat midday sun erases them.
